core: Melody as a succession of pitches through time
supporting: Distinctions between melody, harmony, and rhythm
Repetition and variation of a short melodic idea

Claims that a melodic shape has a universal emotional meaning

claims.claim: Melody is a coherent succession of definite pitches through time, often understood as a tune or musical line.
The cited introductory text identifies range, register, motion, shape, and phrases as features of a melody and notes that melody often has rhythmic organization.
Range is the distance between a melody's lowest and highest pitches, whereas register describes its low, middle, or high pitch area.
Predominantly nearby pitch motion is described as stepwise, while larger skips are described as leaps in the cited introductory discussion.
A melody can be described by its ascending, descending, or mixed contour, and a phrase can be heard as a smaller musical unit with an apparent boundary.
Harmony is the simultaneous combination of notes, which distinguishes it from a melody's successive pitch line.
A motive is a short musical idea that may repeat, and a sequence repeats a motive or phrase at a different pitch level in the cited text.
